title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 34
paragraphs: In the Chersonese, then, the Phoenicians made themselves masters of all the other cities except the city of Cardia. Of these cities up to that time Miltiades son of Cimon, son of Stesagoras, had been tyrant—Miltiades son of Cypselus having acquired this government in the way I shall now describe. The inhabitants of this Chersonese were Dolonkian Thracians; and these Dolonkians, being hard pressed in war by the Apsinthians, sent their kings to Delphi to consult the oracle about the war. The Pythian priestess answered that they should bring into their land as founder of a settlement the man who should first offer them hospitality on their return from the temple. The Dolonkians then traveled along the Sacred Road through the land of the Phocians and Boeotians, and since no man invited them, they turned aside and came to Athens.
